sasha: Heads-up — after enabling FP8-backed KV (int8 decode kernels) on the perf branch I see mixed results. Memory for kv cache dropped ~18% on our wide-ctx tests, but decode stability is worse for some prompts (top-p sampling drift). Latency numbers also shifted for small batches.
kevin: Can you paste the top-line numbers + config? which kernel chooser did you use?
sasha: Sure. Quick summary:
- model: redwood-small-v2, seq=4096, kv enabled on 4 GPUs
- config: kernel_policy=auto, prefer_int8=true, kv_quant=fp8-backed (per-layer scale stored as int8), batch=1/4/16 tested
- baseline (fp16 kv): mem_kv=12.0GB, p95_decode=84ms (batch=1)
- fp8-kv+int8-decode: mem_kv=9.8GB, p95_decode=90ms (batch=1), p95_decode=86ms (batch=4)
- qual: eval perplexity +2.3% on prompt-set-A, sample-consistency diffs for ~6% of prompts
kevin: Hmm. So memory win but small latency regression at small batch sizes. Could be cache unpacking overhead or extra dequant pass. Any kernel-switch counts in trace?
sasha: I grabbed a flame for a single decode. The hot path shows additional memcpy + dequant step before matmul for KV lookup. Patch trace:```
[  hot ] dequantize_kv (8.2ms)
[  hot ] int8_gemm (12.6ms)
[  hot ] kv_merge (3.1ms)
[  hot ] attention (24.1ms)
```
So dequantize_kv is new. For batch>8 the amortization helps and overall token/sec is better. Small-batch sensitive.
maya: Did you try keeping KV in fp8 format on-device and run int8 gemm with quantized kernels that accept fp8 inputs directly? We experimented with fused dequant+matmul kernel that avoids full buffer expansion.
sasha: Tried the fused kernel in the branch but saw numerical divergence on long-decode (>512 tokens) for a few prompts. I suspect rounding bias accumulates.
priyanka: For the quality regression: what calibration procedure was used? Per-layer affine vs global scale? We found per-channel 8-bit scale reduced decode noise vs per-tensor for KV.
sasha: Using per-tensor scale from quick calibration (1000 random KV vectors). I can re-run per-channel calibration but it takes longer.
kevin: Also think about hysteresis in kernel selection. If we have a metric that tracks decode divergence (e.g., token-level KL vs fp16 reference) and switch back to fp16 for problematic requests, we can get mem win for most and quality fallback for some. Add a buffer to avoid flapping.
priyanka: Agree. Implementation idea: maintain per-model per-workload scoring bucket (recent 1000 requests) with fields: avg_KL, p95_latency, mem_savings. If avg_KL>threshold then route to fp16 for that key.
maya: Another operational knob: keep per-request flag for allow_quant_kv. For high-SLO routes (chat interactive) default to fp16 kv, while batch-embedding pipelines get kv-quant.
perf-bot: perf job finished: artifact redwood/kv-quant/1978765432/ — bench matrix uploaded (timeseries + flamegraphs). Link: https://perf.internal/r/1978765432
sasha: Thanks. Next steps for me: 1) rerun with per-channel calibration and larger sample for scales 2) test fused dequant+matmul with rounding-mode tweaks 3) prototype hysteresis routing metric (kevin/priyanka offered to help)
kevin: I'll take the hysteresis prototype. Can you add a small reproducible test case that shows the KL jump? even 10 failing prompts is fine.
sasha: Will add a test in the kv-quant-smoke suite and drop the link here when ready.
priyanka: If per-channel helps, we should measure calibration time tradeoffs vs memory saving — maybe offer two calibration profiles: fast (per-tensor) and accurate (per-channel). Document in rollout notes.
sasha: Yep. I'll add rollout notes and a suggested default: enable kv-quant on non-interactive routes + gradual canary for 10% traffic with default fallback to fp16 when KL>0.02.
maya: Also log warning events when dequant step exceeds X ms for batch=1 routes so SLO team can track.
sasha: Cool. Posting PR shortly with the per-channel calib experiments and a smoke test. cc @kevin @priyanka
kevin: :thumbsup: keep the perf artifacts linked to the PR so we can review flamegraphs quickly.
priyanka: Thanks all — this looks like a path to preserve most wins without regressions.
sasha: End of thread (will update with PR and artifact links).
